brief:
The gravest threat facing Gaza today extends beyond the resumption of conventional warfare that characterized three years of airstrikes and destruction, according to Shehab Wire. Israeli occupation has successfully engineered a new formula for conflict—one generating less international outcry while proving equally lethal to the population.

The shift reflects a strategic recalibration away from high-intensity operations toward methods designed to minimize global attention. This approach maintains sustained pressure on Gaza's population and infrastructure through mechanisms less visible to the international community than the large-scale bombing campaigns that dominated the conflict's earlier phase.
